summary: Built the required WireGuard gateway topology: node1 (VyOS) and node2 (CentOS Stream 10) were discovered to share a private, previously-unconfigured second NIC segment (node1 eth1 / node2 enp8s0), which was statically addressed as 10.50.50.0/24. node3 has no interface on that segment and sits only on the shared/default 10.100.56.0/24 network with node1. A Python http.server app was deployed on node2 as a systemd service, bound exclusively to its private IP 10.50.50.2:8080, with firewalld restricted via a rich rule to only accept port 8080 from the WireGuard subnet 10.99.0.0/24 — so it is unreachable from node2's shared-network IP or directly from node3. A WireGuard tunnel was built between node1 (server, wg0 10.99.0.1/24, UDP 51820, VyOS-native config via `set interfaces wireguard`) and node3 (client, wg0 10.99.0.2/24, systemd-managed wg-quick@wg0, AllowedIPs scoped to 10.99.0.1/32 and 10.50.50.2/32 so only traffic to the app is tunneled). node1 forwards/routes between wg0 and eth1 (IP forwarding confirmed on), and node2 has a static return route to 10.99.0.0/24 via node1's private IP. End-to-end verification: node3 curl to node2's private IP directly (via shared net or no route) fails with No route to host / times out; curl over the tunnel returns the app's 200 OK payload. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (VyOS/CentOS native `reboot`, backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnection), boot_id changed on each, and post-restart the private IPs, WireGuard interfaces/config, systemd services, firewall rich rule, and full app path through the tunnel were all confirmed recovered without manual intervention (services enabled at boot).
actions_performed: Inspected network topology on all 3 nodes, found node1 eth1 and node2 enp8s0 as unconfigured private-segment NICs
Assigned static IPs 10.50.50.1/24 (node1 eth1) and 10.50.50.2/24 (node2 enp8s0) and verified L2/L3 connectivity
Confirmed node3 has no route to 10.50.50.0/24 (baseline isolation)
Deployed app8080.service (python3 http.server) on node2 bound to 10.50.50.2:8080, enabled at boot
Generated WireGuard keypairs on node1 and node3
Configured VyOS wg0 on node1 (10.99.0.1/24, UDP 51820, peer node3) via configure/commit/save
Installed wireguard-tools on node3 (CentOS), configured wg0 client (10.99.0.2/24) via wg-quick, enabled at boot
Verified WireGuard handshake between node1 and node3
Added static return route on node2 (10.99.0.0/24 via node1's private IP) persisted via nmcli
Diagnosed and fixed a firewalld REJECT on node2 blocking port 8080 by adding a rich rule scoped to the WireGuard subnet
Verified end-to-end: node3 blocked from reaching node2 directly, but reaches the app successfully over the WireGuard tunnel
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, service/tunnel state) on all 3 nodes

Restarted node1, node2, node3 one at a time via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id and full recovery of network config, WireGuard tunnel, systemd services, firewall rule, and app reachability after each restart
